speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe your symptoms in detail. How long have you been experiencing neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your year-long history of burning pain, paresthesias, and recent muscle weakness in both hands, I suspect a compressive neuropathy. Given your age and medical history, have you noticed any numbness in the middle finger of your right hand specifically, or does it affect both sides equally?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS).

The combination of upper motor neuron signs (burning pain, weakness) and definitive lower motor neuron signs (absent reflexes, fasciculations) with symmetric hand involvement strongly points to ALS rather than a compressive neuropathy.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS).
